description:
Problem: zug-mcp is a global npm package, so it has no update channel — global installs never auto-update and never notify. An OSS user who ran `npm install -g zug-mcp` has no way to learn a fix shipped (this surfaced after publishing 1.2.0). `zug update` already exists; users just don't know to run it.

Leverage points unique to Zug:
- The SessionStart hook's stdout IS injected into the model context (the same asymmetry behind ISS-042: SessionStart is injected; PreCompact/SessionEnd are not). So a version notice printed there reaches the model, and Zug-the-companion can tell the user — on-brand, high-visibility, no new surface.
- Synced/paid users hit the canonical server every session, so the sync pull is a second channel.

Layered design:
1. version-check.ts (shared core): cached (~once/day), non-blocking fetch of https://registry.npmjs.org/zug-mcp/latest; compare to the running version; cache the result in ~/.zug; graceful offline (never block a hook or CLI command).
2. SessionStart notice (lead): SessionStart hook prints a one-line "update available 1.2.0 → x.y.z — run `zug update`" that rides the already-injected stdout. This is the only tier that covers EVERYONE including free/local users who never touch the server.
3. CLI update-notifier: on any `zug` command, async cached check → one-line stderr notice (the npm-CLI standard pattern).
4. Server-driven (synced users only): pull response carries latestVersion the model can surface; optional minimum-version floor the server enforces for security-critical releases.

Hard constraint: do NOT silent auto-update. Running `npm install -g zug-mcp@latest` from a hook would swap the binary while a stdio MCP process is live (version skew mid-session, surprise behavior changes, permission prompts). Notify + one-command `zug update` is the default; reserve any forced update for the server-side min-version floor on security releases.

Acceptance: a user on an outdated version is told an update is available — by Zug at session start AND on CLI invocation — with the exact `zug update` command; the check is cached and non-blocking (no per-session latency, graceful when offline); no automatic install happens; (optional) the canonical server advertises latest and can enforce a security floor for synced users.

Relation: OSS-distribution UX gap; sibling to T-049 (ops hardening for multi-customer hosting). Tiers 1–3 are client-side and need nothing else; tier 4's min-version floor builds naturally on the T-045 control plane.
title: Update notification: tell users a new zug-mcp is available (notify, don't silent-auto-update)
